transcript: Yesterday, I went to see The Honey Trap by Leo McGann. It was my first time at Irish Rep actually, but I'll definitely be going back — I thought the theatre was lovely and better yet, so was the play. The premise of The Honey Trap is that a man named Dave is giving an interview to a historian about one fateful night in 1979. As British soldiers at the time, he and his friend Bobby were deployed to Northern Ireland during The Troubles. They were out for drinks off duty, they met a couple of women, but their night ended in a way they could’ve never guessed. This play is deceptively simple — it's clear in its storytelling, but it smartly layers different time periods, locations, and revelations in a way that keeps you guessing without leaving you out to dry. It ends up being a bit of a thriller, and while things do come to an appropriate conclusion of sorts, I was left with a really satisfying ambiguity about multiple characters. There's some interesting stuff to think about regarding morality, guilt, and trauma, but the play is definitely plot forward — it invokes questions but avoids getting too bogged down by them. Michael Hayden plays Dave and he's great, as is everyone else in the cast. The scene work feels immediate and the stakes feel effortlessly high the entire time. The Honey Trap is running through November 9th at Irish Rep. With that, another program for my collection.
